card.statement:
Let $R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n)$ be the algebra generated by $\mathbb{C}S_{n}$ and $\mathbb{C}[z_{1},\ldots,z_{n}]$ over $\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]$ subject to the relations

$s_{i}z_{j}=z_{s_{i}(j)}s_{i}+\kappa(\delta_{i+1,j}-\delta_{i,j}).$

We denote by ${R}^{r}_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n)$ the quotient of $R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n)$ by the ideal generated by $\prod_{i=1}^{r}(z_{1}-a_{i})$.

For every $i=0,1,\ldots,r-1$ consider the usual Specht module $S_{n_{i}}\curvearrowright S(\lambda^{i})$, corresponding to $\lambda^{i}$. We can extend $S(\lambda^{i})\otimes\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{i}]$ to the $R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{i}]}(n_{i})$ -module by letting $z_{1}$ act via the multiplication by $a_{i}$. Note that we have the natural embedding

$R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n_{0},\ldots,n_{r-1}):=\\
=R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1}]}(n_{0})\otimes_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa]}\ldots\otimes_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa]}R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{r}]}(n_{r-1})\subset R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n),$

induced by the embedding $S_{n_{0}}\times\ldots\times S_{n_{r-1}}\subset S_{n}$. Then we define

$\widetilde{S}_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(\boldsymbol{\lambda}):=R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n)\otimes_{R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n_{0},\ldots,n_{r-1})}\\
\otimes\Big((S({\lambda^{0}})\otimes\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1}])\otimes_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa]}\ldots\otimes_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa]}(S(\lambda^{r-1})\otimes\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{r}])\Big)$

that is an ${R}^{r}_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a_{1},\ldots,a_{r}]}(n)$ -module. Modding out by $(a_{1}+\ldots+a_{r})$

we obtain the desired $R^{r}(n)$ -module $\widetilde{S}_{\bf{k}}({\boldsymbol{\lambda}})$.

Let us now compute the action of $Z(R^{r}(n))^{JM}$ on $\widetilde{S}_{\bf{k}}(\boldsymbol{\lambda})$. We start with the following lemma. Let $\mu$ be a partition of some $m\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geqslant 1}$ and consider the action $R_{\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a]}(m)\curvearrowright S(\mu)\otimes\mathbb{C}[\kappa,a]$. Recall that $S(\mu)$ has a basis labeled by the standard Young tableaux. such that $JM_{i}$ act on such vectors with the content of $i^{\prime}s$ entry.

paper.title: Hikita-Nakajima conjecture for the Gieseker variety
paper.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{M}_0$ be an affine Nakajima quiver variety, and $\mathcal{M}$ is the corresponding BFN Coulomb branch. Assume that $\mathfrak{M}_0$ can be resolved by the (smooth) Nakajima quiver variety $\mathfrak{M}$. The Hikita-Nakajima conjecture claims that there should be an isomorphism of (graded) algebras $H^*_{S}(\mathfrak{M},\mathbb{C}) \simeq \mathbb{C}[\mathcal{M}_{\mathfrak{s}}^{\mathbb{C}^\times}]$, here $S \curvearrowright \mathfrak{M}_0$ is a torus acting on $\mathfrak{M}_0$ preserving the Poisson structure, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathfrak{s}}$ is the (Poisson) deformation of $\mathcal{M}$ over $\mathfrak{s}=\operatorname{Lie} (S)$, $\mathbb{C}^\times$ is a generic one-dimensional torus acting on $\mathcal{M}$, and $\mathbb{C}[\mathcal{M}_{\mathfrak{s}}^{\mathbb{C}^\times}]$ is the algebra of schematic $\mathbb{C}^\times$-fixed points of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathfrak{s}}$. We prove the Hikita-Nakajima conjecture for $\mathfrak{M}=\mathfrak{M}(n,r)$ Gieseker variety ($ADHM$ space). We produce the isomorphism explicitly on generators. We also describe the Hikita-Nakajima isomorphism above using the realization of $\mathcal{M}_{\mathfrak{s}}$ as the spectrum of the center of rational Cherednik algebra corresponding to $S_n \ltimes (\mathbb{Z}/r\mathbb{Z})^n$ and identify all the algebras that appear in the isomorphism with the center of degenerate cyclotomic Hecke algebra (generalizing some results of Shan, Varagnolo, and Vasserot).
